rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2 Method <U+2013> data collected through semi-structured interviews with 82 farmers and managers of 5 WUAs in summers 2011<U+2013>2012, plus WUA internal documents and field observations. Q2: Section 4.2 Changes in operating rules <U+2013> after drip installation new rules were implemented to distribute water (Vall d'Uix<U+00F3> daily maximum with automatic valve closure; a JTC WUA volume threshold above which price rises; ARJ per-plot flow-rate limit with technical guidelines checked before connection); Section 4.1 <U+2013> WUAs now set irrigation schedules by area and crop; Section 5.1 <U+2013> drip triggered merging of groundwater associations (19 to 12 in Vall d'Uix<U+00F3>), share ceding to WUAs in JTC, and concentration of management in the ARJ Governing Board. Q5: Sections 4.2 and 5.1 report the new rules and organisational changes separately for each of the three distinct irrigation systems (JTC, ARJ, Vall d'Uix<U+00F3>), which differ in water source, size and institutional history (Table 1). Q6: results are reported at irrigation district/WUA scale (schemes of 2,395<U+2013>19,437 ha, Table 1), not at plot level.
rows.notes: Q3: the result rests on interviews (farmers and managers are the same method); WUA documents and field observations are described only as contextual information, so not counted as a second independent method. Q4: the study links automation/remote control to centralized decision-making but this is qualitative description from interviews, not a measured intermediate variable. Q5: the three systems are all in the Valencia region (same climate), but are distinct irrigation districts with per-case results; rated yes on that basis with some doubt. Q7: authors note that where automation/remote control exists it is 'easier' to centralize decisions and that remote control 'facilitates' centralization, which reads as a factor the effect varies with rather than a stated requirement; no requirement for the new allocation rules is stated. Q8: no explicit limitations of the sample, method or sites are stated. Q9: no dispersion measures.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2 Method <U+2013> own semi-structured interviews with 82 farmers (70 with drip) and managers of 5 WUAs. Q2: Section 3.2 Farmer's perspectives <U+2013> first reason for adopting drip was WUA obligation (50%), then increased production (16%); only 9% mentioned water saving; other drivers were product quality, convenience, labour and economic savings. Section 4.2 <U+2013> a technician practises 'psychological irrigation' beyond crop needs to avoid complaints; managers report farmers in some sectors using the same water as before drip and are given additional water on demand. Section 6 <U+2013> when these operating procedures are applied the water-saving potential of drip vanishes; practices fit productivity and convenience goals. Q6: findings are reported at WUA/sector scale across three collective irrigation systems (Table 1), e.g. managers' statement that in transformed sectors most farmers use the same water as before.
rows.notes: The study's own evidence supports the first sentence of the passage (farmer motivations and practices); the basin-scale part of the passage is attributed to another reference and the study provides no water-use measurements. Q3: single method (interviews); no measured water-use data to triangulate. Q4: no measured intermediate variable (water applied vs. crop requirement) <U+2013> statements are qualitative reports by managers and farmers. Q5: motivation percentages are pooled across the 70 drip farmers, not reported per system. Q7: a manager's remark that WUAs will probably have to pressure farmers to reduce demand in order to realise water savings is reported, but the authors do not state it as a requirement from their findings; the observation that withdrawals fall where agro-social factors prevent expansion is cited from other work. Q8: no limitations stated. Q9: only simple percentages, no dispersion measures.

notes: Full text appears complete. Qualitative interview-based study of three collective irrigation systems in Valencia; no quantitative water-use measurements of its own.
